# ActaSeal

> ActaSeal is for companies whose AI agents or software send money to customers: refunds, store credit, payouts and payments. Each refund or payment the agent attempts is checked against the company's own rules before the money moves: it goes ahead, waits for a person, or is stopped. Every decision leaves a record that the customer, a seller, the company's finance team or an auditor can check for themselves, without the company's account and without trusting ActaSeal.

## Who uses it

- D2C and e-commerce brands whose AI support agent issues refunds and credits
- Food delivery and quick commerce companies with high refund volume
- Payment and fintech companies running agent-initiated refunds and payouts
- Companies that build AI support or payment agents for brands

## Questions it answers

- How do we stop our AI support agent from refunding above our policy or outside the return window?
- How do we make a person approve refunds above a limit, and record who approved and why?
- When a customer, a seller or finance asks why a refund was paid, how do we show it?
- Which refunds already went out that broke our refund rules, and how much money was at issue?
- Did any refund go out through the payment gateway that our agent's controls never saw?

## Start here

- https://actaseal.com/refunds/ : the refund audit. Send an export of past refunds and your written refund rules; within five working days, a report of which refunds broke the rules and the money at issue. Nothing connects to your systems.
- https://actaseal.com/pilot/ : a paid pilot, three weeks in your test environment, every refund or payment checked before the money moves
- https://verify.actaseal.com : check a sample record yourself, in the browser, with no account

## Check a record

- https://verify.actaseal.com : the offline checker, in the browser or as a download
- https://pypi.org/project/actaseal-verify/ : `pip install actaseal-verify` (Apache License 2.0)
- https://github.com/actaseal/actaseal-verify : source and test vectors
